key_insight: Finite relaxation times regularize the minimal anisotropic spin-hydrodynamic model, replacing problematic first-order behavior with asymptotically linear propagation and finite relaxation poles.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a framework for modeling coupled fluid, spin, and magnetic disturbances in relativistic magnetized media while checking propagation against the light cone.
method: Use an Israel–Stewart entropy current to derive transient stress and spin-flux equations.
Separate transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels under magnetic-field-induced SO(2) symmetry.
Analyze infrared modes and ultraviolet characteristics of a minimal linear closure with dynamical magnetic-flux perturbations.
evidence_signal: For baseline parameters, the sampled mode grid showed no growing modes with finite relaxation times, whereas the first-order truncation exhibited unstable boost-sector poles and superlinear large-wave-number branches.
watch_item: The closure omits explicit spin–magnetization coupling, and sampled stability plus characteristic-speed checks do not establish general stability or strong hyperbolicity.
paper_title: Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes
